newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary chooses two for final bid on K&H bank sale.
newsitem.headline: Hungary chooses two for final bid on K&H bank sale.

text.p: Hungarian privatisation agency APV Rt has chosen the Bank of Ireland and a Belgian-Irish consortium as final bidders for Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank (K&H), the Hungarian news agency said.
The Bank of Ireland and the consortium, which consists of Belgium's Kredietbank and Irish Life, were selected from a field of five, MTI said.
APV officials were not immediately available for comment.
Hungary has said it will sell a stake of at least 25 percent plus one vote in K&H to a strategic investor who may invite a partner to raise bank equity by at least $30 million.
Earlier press reports said other potential bidders included ING Bank and Austria's Creditanstalt.
According to MTI, both the investors invited to the final round expressed the wish to turn K&H into a universal bank with a leading position in central and eastern Europe.
It said that the Bank of Ireland wanted to acquire more than 75 percent of K&H while the Belgian consortium was targeting a majority stake.
